headline: Technology investment is rising across media, gaming, publishing and education while revenue trends diverge.
summary: Media & Entertainment shows strong top‑line growth and heavy AI spending, but cost pressures appear at WBD. Gaming mixes a revenue‑rich but loss‑making Caesars with high‑margin operators expanding cashless platforms. Publishing is split between a struggling Scholastic and a growing Pearson that is buying AI‑focused assets. Education benefits from large AI and quantum projects and solid revenue at Pearson.

industries.summary: Disney posted 7% revenue growth and a 21% jump in operating income, backed by multiple AI patents and a $20 M AI acquisition. WBD raised its EBITDA outlook but is tightening spend and cutting costs. Versant remains stable with digital‑first strategy. Overall sentiment is upbeat.

leaders.why: Largest revenue ($25,248 m) and strong operating margin growth

laggards.why: Lowest margin (6.9%) and negative YoY revenue

themes.title: AI & tech investment
themes.detail: Companies are buying AI tools, filing patents and embedding AI in theme‑park experiences.

themes.title: Cost discipline
themes.detail: WBD launched a voluntary buyout program targeting $6 bn savings.

industries.it_note: Disney plans to expand AI spend, WBD is tightening, while Cox and LA Times have unclear plans.

industries.summary: Caesars generated $2.94 bn revenue but widened its net loss. Bally’s grew 20% YoY with expanding interactive bets. Light & Wonder posted the highest margin (26.9%) and is rolling out cashless payment platforms. Brightstar remains neutral.

laggards.why: Lowest revenue ($584 m) and declining YoY growth

themes.title: Digital platform rebuild
themes.detail: Light & Wonder launches RAPIDPLAY cashless system across Nevada casinos.

themes.title: Vendor partnerships
themes.detail: Bally’s uses ForceIQ data platform and secures tech contracts for new casino projects.

industries.it_note: Bally’s is expanding spend, Light & Wonder is tightening, Caesars' outlook is unclear.

industries.summary: Wolters Kluwer is expanding AI tools but gave no financial detail. Scholastic missed revenue and posted a large operating loss. Pearson accelerated revenue growth and cut profit guidance while buying AI assessment firms.

leaders.why: Largest disclosed revenue ($1,779 m) and positive margin

laggards.why: Revenue miss ($216.8 m) and deep operating loss

themes.title: AI & tech investment
themes.detail: Wolters Kluwer launched AI tax and legal tools; Pearson acquired AI assessment companies.

industries.it_note: Both Wolters Kluwer and Pearson are increasing AI spend; no contrary signals.

industries.summary: Pearson continues strong revenue growth and AI acquisitions. NYU secured city‑backed funding for a $284 m quantum fabrication facility. SLU deepened its AI partnership with World Wide Technology. ACT provides neutral testing data.

leaders.why: Highest revenue ($1,779 m) and expanding margin

laggards.why: No revenue disclosed and neutral performance

themes.title: AI & quantum investment
themes.detail: NYU receives up to $284 m for quantum labs; SLU partners on AI research.

industries.it_note: All players are increasing spend on AI, quantum and technology collaborations.
